summary: The subject check accepts the subject entity's name or any of its tags, compared with whitespace removed from both sides; the skill says where the source's other forms go.
why: Run-10 refused 35 of its 130 subjects with SUBJECT_NOT_NAMED. Classified from the capture: 14 genuinely unnamed in the sentence that formalizes them, 7 aliases ("Mid-Atlantic Ridge" named, "the MAR" written), 8 partial names ("Oceanic crust" named, "crust" written), 6 whitespace artefacts ("CO2" named, the text layer printing "CO 2"). Twenty-one of the thirty-five are the check being more literal than names are and none is a wrong subject: a source uses a short form after introducing a thing in full. The adapter now reads every form the subject record carries, its name and each member of tags, and accepts a statement that writes any of them; both sides drop whitespace rather than collapsing it, case-folded as before, so a name the text layer breaks matches its own bytes. tags is a root slot on Describable, which Entity mixes in, so no slot is added. SUBJECT_NOT_NAMED stands and names every form tried. Decision 20 carries the limits: no fuzzy or semantic matching, a pronoun or an unrepeated antecedent still leaves subject unset and the census counts it, the residual 14, and a tag is not a second name for query projection. Additive, so research stays at 0.5.0.
